lines.text: They told me you were *dead.*
Every night after that, we talked through the hatch. In Morse. One letter at a time.
It took an hour to say one sentence. We had all night.
Her name was Mara Lind. Mission specialist.
A biologist. She had been growing plants in Module 3 when the alarm went off.
Her day one sounded like mine. The same alarm. The same leak.
Her capsule had a seat with a red tag. No go.
And her commander said: everyone on that side is gone.
On her side, our side was the one that leaked.
He meant me.
Her gauge read zero too.
Two gauges. Both pointing at zero. Both lying.
Then she told me about her letter.
Three rules. Never open Hatch 3. Not for anyone.
Same words. Same handwriting.
Signed: Hale.
The man who wrote my rules wrote hers.
She'd knocked for thirty nights. Nobody answered.
I thought I was going crazy, she said. So on day seventy, she stopped.
She'd done the same math as me. The same tank. The same 1.7 kilos.
Two people, breathing from one tank, each thinking the other was a ghost.
Day one hundred eighty. Envelope six.
If you've found each other, don't say it out loud. They're watching.
They.
Who were they?
That night, Mara knocked a new message.
There is a camera in my room.
I looked up at the smoke detector over my bunk.
A tiny red *light.*
